title: In Luke 11 What Does Jesus Response To The Pharisees Reveal About The Nature Of His Ministry
paragraphs: Introduction: Jesus and the Pharisees in Luke 11

In Luke 11, Jesus engages in a powerful dialogue with the Pharisees and experts in the law. His responses are not only a critique of religious hypocrisy but also a profound revelation of the true nature of His ministry. By examining this passage, we gain insight into Christ’s mission, His call for genuine righteousness, and the transformative power of the gospel.
Context: The Setting of Luke 11

After teaching His disciples to pray, Jesus is invited to dine with a Pharisee. What follows is a series of confrontations, as Jesus exposes the underlying issues within the Pharisaic approach to religion. This passage is found in Luke 11, especially verses 37-54.
Jesus’ Response: Exposing the Heart
The Pharisees are offended that Jesus does not observe their ritual hand-washing before the meal. Jesus responds by addressing the heart of the matter:
Now ye Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter; but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness. - Luke 11:39 ASV
Jesus reveals that His ministry is not about external conformity, but about inner transformation. True holiness begins in the heart, not merely in outward rituals (see also Matthew 23:25-26 ASV).
Woes to the Pharisees: The Danger of Hypocrisy
Jesus pronounces several woes upon the Pharisees, highlighting their misplaced priorities:
But woe unto you Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and every herb, and pass over justice and the love of God: but these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. - Luke 11:42 ASV

He criticizes their focus on minor rules while neglecting “justice and the love of God.” Jesus’ ministry emphasizes the heart of the Law: loving God and others (Matthew 22:37-40 ASV). External acts of piety, when disconnected from love and justice, miss the point of God’s commands.
The Centrality of Repentance and Grace
Jesus’ confrontations reveal that His ministry is about calling people to repentance and inviting them into God’s grace. He exposes sin not to shame, but to invite transformation:

Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send unto them prophets and apostles; and some of them they shall kill and persecute; that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation. - Luke 11:49 ASV

Jesus places Himself in the line of rejected prophets, showing that His ministry fulfills God’s redemptive plan. Yet, He also offers hope: through faith in Him, one can be forgiven and cleansed (John 1:12 ASV; Luke 19:10 ASV).
The Authority of Christ’s Ministry

Throughout Luke 11, Jesus speaks with divine authority, interpreting the Law perfectly and exposing the need for a Savior. His rebuke of the Pharisees’ traditions underscores that He is the fulfillment of the Law and the prophets (Matthew 5:17 ASV). Jesus alone has the authority to define true righteousness.
Application: The Call to Authentic Faith

Jesus’ response challenges His followers to pursue authentic faith—a faith marked by inner transformation, love, and humility before God. Outward religious acts have value only when they flow from a heart changed by grace (Romans 12:1-2 ASV). Believers are called to examine their motives and seek a relationship with God that transforms every aspect of life.
Conclusion

In Luke 11, Jesus’ interactions with the Pharisees illuminate the heart of His ministry: a call to genuine righteousness, reliance on grace, and transformation from the inside out. The passage reminds us that Christ came not to reform religion, but to redeem hearts, offering forgiveness and new life to all who believe.
